identity: A student argumentative essay titled Silah dhu haddayn (a double-edged sword), on social media: title line, a short opening paragraph, and one long 211-token body paragraph running from the positive case (intellectual growth, time management, social progress) to the negative one (wasted time, spread of conflict and crime) and a closing recommendation.
law: PROSE, essay register. Only three <NL> so PASS 0 gives almost nothing. The unit is the orthographic sentence and the batch-12 correction governs: a COORDINATOR heading a new finite clause cuts (f + verb, w + verb, lakin), a SUBORDINATOR does not (illa anna, li-anna, alladhi, idha, in, ala al-raghm min). 276 real tokens / 22 units = 12.5 per unit, at the fine end of the prose band, which suits the short-sentence student register.
reasoning: The essay is built on fronted discourse frames and they decide most of the boundaries - every one of them takes the cut BEFORE it, never after (0n/0x): @88 before fa-ala sabil al-mithal, @158 before ala al-raghm min, @189 before fa-huna (the C8/G4 deictic), @243 before wa-fi al-nihaya. Explanatory fa + a new finite verb cuts, per 1j and its batch-12 evidence fa-huwa yuharib / fa-qad kanat: @11 (fa-l-kathir la yai), @136 (fa-bi-dhalika tandarij). @38/@44 isolate the rhetorical question wa-lakin ma huwa ahaduha ya tura as its own unit - lakin here opens a new move in the argument, which 1q says cuts, and a question is a distinct act. Where I refused: (a) @82 - kayfa yakunu tathiruha ijabiyyan aw salbiyyan wa-dhalika bi-hasab al-shakhs is a rhetorical question with its own answer glued on (C4), and wa-dhalika is anaphoric (0q), so the pair is ONE unit; (b) the whole 25-token conditional @107-@131 (idha kana istikhdamuhu ijabiyyan ... fa-hinaha yaktamil) is one sentence - I must not cut between a protasis and its apodosis, and ay annahu is a demoted subordinator; (c) the 31-token concessive @159-@189 keeps illa inna al-bad yusi istikhdamaha inside it, and the ka-examples (ka-mushahadat, wa-murasalat, wa-ghayriha) are masdars riding in one PP (0t); (d) @141/@143/@153/@156 are all masdar conjuncts and merge, while @146 DOES cut because wa-ala al-mujtama fronts its own PP for a different topic (society, not the individual) - the two halves of the conjunct-weight test in one sentence, as in F8. The one call I am least sure of is @215: al-halak wa-al-daya wa-al-daya al-fikri is a bare fragment listing the outcomes, asyndetic after the proverb al-waqt ka-l-sayf, and I read it as its own unit rather than as the object of qataaka.
